title: The constructed algebra-valued derived Hom adjunction
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $B$ be a commutative algebra sheaf on $Y$ whose underlying structure-sheaf module is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], and assume the chosen derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $D(B)$ exist [def-pc-derived-category], with arbitrary morphism universes. For the explicit algebra-valued derived Hom functor $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(B,-)$ of [def-pc-derived-rhom-algebra-module], there is an adjunction from the rightDerivedFunctor of scalar restriction along $B.hom$ to this constructed functor. This asserts no quasi-coherence or boundedness of its values, and assumes no finiteness or Noetherianity.

source.place: Tags 0BV0 and 0BV1; their argument for general algebra sheaves using Modules Tag 0A6F and Derived Categories Tag 09T5

proof.text: For the explicit sheafAlgebraHom construction, restriction of scalars has right adjoint Hom(B,-). On each smaller open, send an O-linear map phi from restricted M to F to m |-> (b |-> phi(bm)); send a B-linear map psi from M to Hom(B,F) to m |-> psi(m)(1). O-linearity, B-linearity, and compatibility with restrictions follow from the module axioms. The composites are identities: phi(1m)=phi(m), and psi(m)(b)=psi(bm)(1). Naturality under postcomposition and precomposition gives the sheaf adjunction. This is the explicit proof of Modules Tag 0A6F specialized to B.hom; it uses the exact action of the recorded construction, not an arbitrary Hom functor with an isomorphic underlying module.

Restriction along B.hom preserves finite limits and finite colimits, by the two restriction-exactness theorems in def-pc-derived-rhom-algebra-module. Its termwise localization therefore gives the exact derived scalar functor. Exactness also implies that its right adjoint sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes: maps from an acyclic complex into Hom(B,I) correspond to maps from its acyclic scalar restriction into I. Compute the right derived functor using the functorial K-injective resolution of prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist. The result is the localization of the explicit Hom(B,I(-)) construction; derivedRHomAlgebraModule_comparison identifies its factorization with the defining localization of derivedRHomAlgebraModule, preserving B-action.

Apply the derived-adjunction theorem (Stacks Tag 09T5) to the exact scalar-restriction adjunction and the K-injective right derived functor. Both comparisons are absolute: exact restriction descends through quasi-isomorphisms, and K-injective resolutions compute the absolute right derived functor. Uniqueness of the localization lifts identifies the right functor with derivedRHomAlgebraModule. The exact-functor comparison rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies the left functor with the specified rightDerivedFunctor of scalar restriction. Transport the derived adjunction along these two natural isomorphisms to obtain the stated Nonempty adjunction. The argument applies to all complexes; it never uses finite generation, Noetherianity or a bound.

theorem sheafAlgebraDerivedHom_adjunction
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (B : Y.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hB : B.toModule.IsQuasicoherent)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B.right))] :
    Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map B.hom)).rightDerivedFunctor ⊣
          derivedRHomAlgebraModule Y B hB)
